title: Uber Technologies Q3 Earnings Miss on Investment Loss as Bookings Jump 20%
excerpt: Gross bookings hit $59.82 billion and non-GAAP EPS rose 35% to $0.88, but a $476 million investment revaluation loss cut GAAP earnings to $0.25 per share, below estimates.
body:
• Uber's third-quarter gross bookings rose 20% to $59.82 billion — its fifth straight quarter of 20%-plus growth — as trips grew 16% to 4.1 billion and monthly active consumers reached 215 million.
  • Revenue rose 10% to $14.77 billion, just ahead of the Zacks consensus, but GAAP earnings of $0.25 per share missed estimates after a $476 million pre-tax loss from revaluing equity investments; non-GAAP earnings rose 35% to $0.88.
  • Operating profitability kept expanding: non-GAAP operating income jumped 38% to $2.30 billion, a record 3.9% of gross bookings, adjusted EBITDA rose 31% to $2.96 billion, and free cash flow was $2.54 billion.
  • For the fourth quarter Uber guided gross bookings to $63.25–$65.25 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $0.95–$0.99, and expects about 700 fully driverless vehicles on the platform by year-end.

Uber Technologies reported a mixed third quarter on November 4: demand and operating profit grew at record pace, while investment losses cut reported earnings well below Wall Street's expectations. In its results release, the San Francisco company said gross bookings grew 20% year over year to $59.82 billion and revenue grew 10% to $14.77 billion, slightly ahead of the $14.74 billion Zacks Consensus Estimate. GAAP earnings, however, came in at $0.25 per share against a 94-cent consensus, Zacks reported.

The miss is an accounting story more than an operating one. GAAP net income fell to $512 million from $6.63 billion a year earlier, a comparison distorted on both sides: this year's figure includes a $476 million pre-tax net loss from revaluations of Uber's equity investments, while the year-ago quarter included large tax and investment gains. On the non-GAAP measures management steers by, net income rose 29% to $1.80 billion and earnings per share rose 35% to $0.88.

"Uber delivered its fifth consecutive quarter of 20%+ Gross Bookings growth, driven by record audience and consumer engagement."

— Dara Khosrowshahi, Uber CEO

All three businesses grew bookings

Mobility gross bookings rose 18% to $29.51 billion, Delivery rose 22% to $28.54 billion and Freight rose 35% to $1.77 billion. Reported revenue told a different story for the largest business: Mobility revenue fell 2% to $7.52 billion because business-model changes cut total reported revenue growth by eight percentage points, the company said, even as Mobility's segment operating income rose 27% to $2.36 billion. Delivery revenue jumped 23% to $5.49 billion with segment operating income up 30% to $1.06 billion, and Freight revenue rose 34% to $1.76 billion while its operating loss narrowed to $33 million.

Usage set records across the platform. Trips increased 16% to 4.06 billion, monthly active platform consumers rose 14% to 215 million, and monthly trips per consumer improved 2%. GAAP income from operations rose 30% to $1.45 billion, adjusted EBITDA rose 31% to $2.96 billion, and Uber ended the quarter with $10.1 billion in unrestricted cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments.

Guidance and the autonomy push

For the fourth quarter, Uber expects gross bookings of $63.25 billion to $65.25 billion, growth of 18% to 22% in constant currency with an expected currency headwind of about one percentage point, non-GAAP earnings of $0.95 to $0.99 per share, and adjusted EBITDA of $3.13 billion to $3.23 billion. Khosrowshahi said the company's autonomous-vehicle focus is shifting to commercial execution, with approximately 700 fully driverless vehicles expected on Uber by year-end and more than 2,000 in 2027. Coverage of the outlook also noted headwinds management flagged, including the drag from the Middle East conflict on Mobility bookings growth — about 75 basis points in the third quarter and an assumed 100 basis points in the fourth. The fourth-quarter report, due in February, will test both the bookings range and that autonomy timetable.
